Any living thing, such as a plant, an animal or a fungus.
Example: A tree is an organism.
cards.say: organism. Any living thing, such as a plant, an animal or a fungus. Example: A tree is an organism.

cards.back:
All the living things in a place and the non-living things around them.
Example: A pond is an ecosystem.
cards.say: ecosystem. All the living things in a place and the non-living things around them. Example: A pond is an ecosystem.

cards.back:
A living thing so small that you need a microscope to see it.
Example: Bacteria are microorganisms.
cards.say: microorganism. A living thing so small that you need a microscope to see it. Example: Bacteria are microorganisms.

cards.back:
A substance that living things need to grow and stay healthy.
Example: Protein is a nutrient.
cards.say: nutrient. A substance that living things need to grow and stay healthy. Example: Protein is a nutrient.

cards.back:
What is needed to make things happen. It cannot be made or destroyed.
Example: Food gives your body energy.
cards.say: energy. What is needed to make things happen. It cannot be made or destroyed. Example: Food gives your body energy.

cards.back:
A push or a pull.

cards.say: force. A push or a pull. Example: Gravity is a force that pulls things down.

cards.back:
What an object is made from.
Example: Glass is a material.
cards.say: material. What an object is made from. Example: Glass is a material.

cards.back:
A feature that describes a material, such as hard or flexible.
Example: A property of metal is that it is shiny.
cards.say: property. A feature that describes a material, such as hard or flexible. Example: A property of metal is that it is shiny.

cards.back:
A material that lets heat or electricity pass through it easily.
Example: Copper is a good conductor of electricity.
cards.say: conductor. A material that lets heat or electricity pass through it easily. Example: Copper is a good conductor of electricity.

cards.back:
A material that does not let heat or electricity pass through easily.
Example: Plastic is an electrical insulator.
cards.say: insulator. A material that does not let heat or electricity pass through easily. Example: Plastic is an electrical insulator.

A change that you can undo.

cards.say: reversible change. A change that you can undo. Example: Melting ice is a reversible change.

cards.back:
A change that you cannot undo.
Example: Burning wood is an irreversible change.
cards.say: irreversible change. A change that you cannot undo. Example: Burning wood is an irreversible change.

The curved path of an object moving around a star, a planet or a moon.
Example: Earth takes a year to orbit the Sun.

To turn around a centre, like a spinning top.
Example: Earth rotates once every twenty four hours.
cards.say: rotate. To turn around a centre, like a spinning top. Example: Earth rotates once every twenty four hours.

To bounce back off a surface.
Example: A mirror reflects light.
cards.say: reflect. To bounce back off a surface. Example: A mirror reflects light.

cards.back:
To soak up or take in.

cards.say: absorb. To soak up or take in. Example: A sponge absorbs water.

cards.back:
Letting light pass through so you can see clearly.
Example: A window is transparent.
cards.say: transparent. Letting light pass through so you can see clearly. Example: A window is transparent.

cards.back:
To move quickly backwards and forwards.
Example: A guitar string vibrates when you pluck it.
cards.say: vibrate. To move quickly backwards and forwards. Example: A guitar string vibrates when you pluck it.

cards.back:
To move pollen to a flower so seeds can form.

cards.back:
An animal that hunts other animals for food.

cards.back:
The natural home of a plant or animal.

To mix into a liquid so that you can no longer see the solid.
